newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea blasts Seoul over submarine incursion.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea blasts Seoul over submarine incursion.

text.p: North Korea on Monday accused the rival South of hypocrisy for demanding that Pyongyang apologise for the intrusion of a Northern submarine in September.
"Their demand for an apology from the North, the victim, is gangster-like logic and the height of shamelessness," said a spokesman for the Central Committee of the North Korean Red Cross Society.
The statement was carried by Pyongyang's official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) monitored in Tokyo.

The Shark-class submarine landed 26 North Koreans when it ran aground on South Korea's east coast on September 18. Twenty-four have been shot dead, one was captured alive and another is still at large.
South Korea has demanded that Pyongyang apologise but North Korea insisted the incident was an accident and demanded the return of the vessel, the captured crewmember and the bodies of those killed.
"This (North Korean) demand is reasonable in view of the background of the submarine incident and the principle of Red Cross humanitarianism," the North Korean Red Cross spokesman said.
"It is brigandish for the South Korean authorities to turn down our just demand while urging us to apologise," he said.
"As a matter of fact, it is they who should apologise and ask for a pardon for the submarine incident," he added.
Tension has remained high on the divided Korean peninsula since the submarine incursion.
"Although they (South Koreans) knew that our submarine was wrecked after an accident, they groundlessly branded our soldiers as spies and brutally killed them..." the North Korean spokesman said.
He said Pyongyang had taken "humanitarian" measures to return South Korean intruders and those who were killed in the 1950-53 Korean War.

"In the past, we even sent back dead bodies of those who illegally intruded into our side and committed hostile acts and, furthermore, we have returned remains of those who died more than 40 years ago in the Korean War," he said.
The accusation came only a few hours after the biggest group of North Korean defectors since the war arrived in Seoul.

The 17 escapees, who sneaked into Hong Kong on November 23 after a month-long trek down the length of China, were all related and included a security guard whose job was to stop defectors from crossing the North Korea-China border.
